newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends off on strong US data, outlook muted.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends off on strong US data, outlook muted.

text.p: Shares ended lower after another slow session on Wednesday as better-than-expected U.S. output data in the final hour of trade spoiled earlier attempts at higher ground and caution returned, brokers said.

Forestry major UPM-Kymmene led the market higher earlier, partly boosted by more speculation that it would buy parts of Canadian magazine paper maker Repap, but Nokia was weak all day due to soft technology shares in the U.S..
But prices turned lower late on as U.S. March industrial output rose faster than expected -- 0.9 percent compared to 0.6 percent in February and an average forecast of 0.6 percent.
The HEX general index closed down 0.27 percent at 2,787.16 after trading between 2,778.73 and 2,809.19 points, and the FOX portfolio and derivatives index fell 0.28 percent to 971.02.
The focus was on U.S. reactions to the data, brokers said.
"U.S. manufacturing figures pointed to continued vigour in consumer demand and that may lead to further rate hikes by the Fed," one broker said.
Brokers expected Helsinki to remain quiet as long as the U.S. market suffers from interest rate jitters.
Telecoms giant and bourse engine Nokia was off 3.00 markka or one percent at 294.00 markka, but higher than its 290.10 markka session low.
Forestries outperformed and the sub-index closed a whisker higher as UPM-Kymmene added 1.00 markka to close at 110.00.

Metra rose with Swedish lock maker Assa Abloy, in which it holds a 29 percent stake, on Assa's acquisition of French Vachette. Metra rose 3.50 markka to 141.00, but trade was thin; less than five million markka.
